name: Vanuatu

findings.local_actor: Government of Vanuatu (Ministry of Infrastructure and Utilities)
findings.summary: Huawei built Vanuatu's Government Broadband Network under a 2008 contract financed by a China Eximbank concessional loan: about 100 km of fibre, fixed wireless to roughly 100 government offices, and microwave/VSAT links to provincial capitals; completed July 2012.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary), Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: Huawei supplied the network, so pole prc. Tier 5 for a completed national network; current operational status and vendor role in maintenance not confirmed, so still_current null. Single opened S2 research dataset (it cites the loan agreement and Huawei contract, not opened). Loan face value RMB 200m; not converted at a source-date rate, so values null.

findings.local_actor: Government of Vanuatu (Ministry of Infrastructure and Utilities)
findings.financier: China Export-Import Bank (concessional loan, same as VUT-001)
findings.summary: The same China Eximbank-financed, Huawei-built e-Government project included a government data centre, completed in 2012 alongside the broadband network.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary), Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator rule: the data centre is a Government of Vanuatu facility, so domestic; Huawei is builder and China Eximbank financier, neither sets the pole. If Huawei holds operational access to the facility the pole would be prc; not established. Location not stated by the source.

findings.summary: Reuters reported Huawei earlier supplied crime-reduction digital systems to Port Vila, needing a local data centre; the PM's office said police do not currently use the Huawei surveillance system. The PM toured Huawei policing technology in Shenzhen.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 3 on reported supply of a system to Port Vila; no contract, value or delivery date found, and police non-use suggests it may not be operational for policing. Article undated on the page; context (PM Salwai, Japan Pacific leaders meeting the following week) suggests mid-2024 but date left null. Islands Business carries the same Reuters story, so not independent.

findings.summary: TE SubCom announced a contract in force to build the 1,632 km ICN2 submarine cable for Vanuatu's Interchange Limited, linking Port Vila and Luganville to Honiara, Solomon Islands, with service expected in Q4 2019.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: SubCom (US) supplied the cable, so pole us. Tier 3 (contract in force); ready-for-service not confirmed in this run, so not tier 5. Ocean News echoes the SubCom release, so not independent corroboration; medium on the single opened S1. Pre-2020 and not reconfirmed.

findings.local_actor: Digicel Vanuatu (Digicel Pacific, acquired by Telstra 2022)
findings.summary: Reporting on Telstra's Digicel Pacific takeover said Digicel's 3G and 4G networks across its Pacific markets, including Vanuatu, run on Huawei equipment, which Telstra would keep for now and align with Australian standards only at future refresh.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: Huawei RAN, so pole prc. Region-wide statement, not Vanuatu-specific vendor evidence. The Register (Aug 2025) states Telstra removed Huawei gear after taking control of Digicel; if true for Vanuatu this would be a geopolitical reversal, but no Vanuatu-specific replacement evidence found, so not coded as a reversal.

findings.controller: Not stated (Government of Vanuatu announced the facilities)
findings.summary: Australia committed to help fund two data centres, in Port Vila and on Santo, reported at A$120 million within the A$500 million Nakamal Agreement package, initialled August 2025 and signed 29 June 2026.

sources.publisher: Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: owner-operator not stated; Vanuatu government origin suggests domestic, Australian funding does not set the pole. Tier 1: funding commitment, no contract, builder or vendor named. The signed treaty text (DFAT) does not mention data centres, but Article 8 requires Vanuatu to consult Australia on third-party engagement in critical infrastructure including telecommunications. DCD and Register likely derive from the same announcement, so not counted as corroboration. A$120m converts to about US$79m per The Register; not recorded as value pending source-date conversion.
